newsitem.title: MEXICO: Serfin sharply down on 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Serfin sharply down on 1996 loss.

text.p: Shares listed by Mexican financial group Serfin were sharply down in midday trading on a poor 1996 earnings report, uncertainty over the form of a coming deal with HSBC holdings and a bad loans portfolio sale to the government, traders said.
"The report was very, very bad, just awful," a floor trader in Mexico City said.
"It's also not clear what the shareholding structure will be like after the HSBC deal and the sale to Fobaproa," he added. Analysts have worried about dilution after the sale.
Serfin A and B class shares headed the prominent decliners' list .PL.MX on the Mexican bourse.
The A class was down 17 centavos to 2.30 pesos while the B class was off 11 centavos to 3.09 pesos.

A flurry of news concerning Serfin has broken this week. The banking unit posted a net loss in excess of seven billion pesos for 1996 on Tuesday, on the heels of news it had sold a bad loans portfolio to the government's bank insurance fund.
Serfin also confirmed HSBC holdings was to acquire a 19.9 percent stake in the group.
"It is not a done deal yet, so that leads to uncertainty, and the (1996 earnings) report didn't go down at all well," a desk trader added.

"They did create reserves, but even so the capitalization index was still down. Furthermore, they began hitting it yesterday on Wall Street, and they're doing so again now. It's very volatile," he added.
Serfin ADRs were off 1/8 to 3-5/8 in New York.
